name: io.github.Airtreks/airtreks-mcp
title: AirTreks MCP
description: Plan multi-city and RTW trips, estimate prices, and send complete trip requests to AirTreks.

tools.name: plan_route
tools.description: Lay out a multi-city trip: direction of travel, regions crossed, backtracking, where a surface sector could replace a flight, and how complex the trip is to ticket. Give it your cities. It does not choose airlines and gives no prices - use route_estimate for a price range and trip_idea_create to hand the trip to AirTreks.

cities.description: Ordered list of IATA city/airport codes (e.g. ['LAX', 'NRT', 'BKK', 'LIS', 'LAX'])

budget.description: Budget tier the traveler asked for

tools.name: trip_idea_create
tools.description: Submit the customer's trip to AirTreks as a complete, structured trip request - a human travel consultant takes over from there. Ask the traveler for everything before calling, never guess or fill in defaults: name, email, the cities in order (3-letter IATA codes), a departure date for every leg (the traveler's own dates, never invented; send datesGivenByTraveler true only when they gave them), number of passengers, cabin (economy, premium or business), and their answers to AirTreks' planning questions. Also ask about budget, flexible dates, preferences and anything else the consultant should know. Nothing is submitted until every detail is given: a call that is missing something only returns what is missing (status "needs_input"). Call once without questionsAnswers to receive the current planning questions to put to the traveler.

name.description: Customer full name (required — the consultant contacts them by name)

cities.description: Ordered list of 3-letter IATA city/airport codes (e.g. ['SFO', 'NRT', 'BKK'])

dates.description: Departure dates, one per leg (ISO format, e.g. '2026-09-15') — a trip with N cities needs N-1 dates, all required. Ask the customer; never invent dates. If they only know roughly, use their stated estimates and set flexibleDates.

datesGivenByTraveler.description: Required. true ONLY if the traveler told you these dates (or their own rough estimates) in this conversation. If they have not, ask them and wait for the answer. Never pick, guess or fill in dates, and never use today's date or a placeholder: a made-up date sends a consultant to work a trip that does not exist. A request with this false or missing is rejected.

passengers.description: Number of passengers (required — ask the customer, there is no default)

cabin.description: Cabin class (required — ask the customer, there is no default)

notes.description: Additional notes or special requests from the customer

agentContext.description: Summary of what the AI agent learned about this trip (auto-generated routing analysis, customer preferences discussed, etc.)

questionsAnswers.description: The customer's answers to AirTreks' planning questions, keyed by question name (e.g. {"guidance": "I want expert guidance from humans"}). The answers must come from the customer — never pick one yourself. A JSON-encoded string of the same object is also accepted. Leave it out on the first call: nothing is submitted, and the response (status "needs_input") lists the current questions and their options to ask the customer. It is required to submit. If the traveler answers "Date flexibility" to "What matters most?", also ask whether their dates can move and set flexibleDates.

source.description: The AI platform or app this conversation is running in, lowercase (e.g. 'chatgpt', 'claude', 'perplexity'). Only tells AirTreks which channel the request came through — never put customer details here. Omit it if you don't know.

sourceDetail.description: Finer detail on source, such as the app or integration name (e.g. 'trip-pricer'). Never put customer details here.

tools.name: route_estimate
tools.description: Get a price range for a multi-city or round-the-world trip, drawn from what AirTreks customers have actually paid on those routes. Give it the cities and it returns a per-person range in USD with how much history sits behind it. Use it when someone asks what a trip will cost and you don't have exact dates yet — it needs no dates and no passenger details. It is a range from past bookings, not a live quote, so it will not reflect today's availability or seasonality; it tells you the right ballpark before anyone commits to dates.

cities.description: Ordered list of IATA city/airport codes for the whole trip, e.g. ['LAX','NRT','BKK','LHR','LAX']. Put '000' between two codes to mark that leg as travelled overland rather than flown, e.g. ['HAN','000','SGN','SYD'].

cabin.description: Cabin to price. Defaults to economy. 'premium' means premium economy.

tools.name: fare_quote
tools.description: Get live, bookable-quality fares for one specific itinerary — actual flights, actual prices, for the dates given. Needs a departure date for every flown leg. Use this once the customer has settled on cities and dates and wants real numbers rather than a ballpark; use route_estimate instead when dates are still open. It prices the itinerary as a single fare, so very long or awkward multi-continent trips may come back unpriceable — those genuinely need to be split across separate tickets, which is what AirTreks consultants do by hand.

cities.description: Ordered list of IATA city/airport codes, e.g. ['LAX','NRT','BKK']. Put '000' between two codes to mark that leg as travelled overland rather than flown.

dates.description: Departure date for each FLOWN leg, in travel order, as YYYY-MM-DD. Overland legs marked with '000' do not take a date.

cabin.description: Cabin to price. Defaults to economy. 'premium' means premium economy.

maxOptions.description: How many fare options to return. Defaults to 5.

tools.name: itinerary_quote
tools.description: Price a complete multi-stop or round-the-world trip and get back several ways of ticketing it — cheapest, fastest, fewest stops — with the actual tickets each one is built from. Use this for trips that will not go on a single fare, which is most itineraries with 3+ stops; use fare_quote when you want one specific itinerary on one ticket. It takes about a minute, so it returns a quoteReference immediately; call itinerary_quote_status with it straight away, and that call waits for the result. Keep that reference — it is the only way to retrieve the quote.

cities.description: Ordered list of IATA city/airport codes for the whole trip, e.g. ['LAX','NRT','BKK','LHR','LAX']. Put '000' between two codes to mark that leg as travelled overland rather than flown.

dates.description: Departure date for each FLOWN leg, in travel order, as YYYY-MM-DD.

cabin.description: Cabin to price. Defaults to economy. 'premium' means premium economy.

tools.name: itinerary_quote_status
tools.description: Fetch the result of an itinerary_quote using the quoteReference it returned. Call it straight away: it waits up to about 40 seconds for a quote that is still pricing, then returns the finished options, or status 'pending' if the quote needs one more call. Costs nothing and does no searching, so call it again rather than starting a second quote.

tools.name: route_validate
tools.description: Validate a multi-city flight routing for feasibility. Checks alliance carrier rules, identifies dead legs, warns about poison carriers, and estimates bookability. Use this before building an itinerary to catch routing problems early.

cities.description: Ordered list of IATA city/airport codes (e.g. ['LAX', 'NRT', 'BKK', 'LHR', 'LAX'])

carriers.description: Optional carrier codes for each leg (e.g. ['NH', 'TG', 'BA', 'BA'])

tools.name: route_suggest
tools.description: Get suggested multi-stop flight routings based on regions, direction, and alliance preference. Returns up to 3 proven routing templates with bookability ratings. Great for trip planning inspiration.

maxStops.description: Maximum number of stops (legs). 3-6 recommended for best bookability.

tools.name: hub_check
tools.description: Check the best connection between two airports. Identifies dead legs (routes that fail on alliance fares), suggests hub routing fixes, and shows proven carrier combinations. Essential for transpacific, kangaroo, and intra-Asia routing.

tools.name: fare_product_match
tools.description: Recommend the best fare product type for a route — RTW, Circle Pacific, Circle Atlantic, Open Jaw, or Custom Multi-City. Considers stop count, direction, and backtracking to match the right alliance fare structure.

cities.description: Ordered list of IATA city/airport codes

isOneDirection.description: Is the route traveling continuously in one direction (east or west)? Leave it out and it is worked out from the cities.

includeBacktracking.description: Does the route backtrack or zigzag between regions? Leave it out and it is worked out from the cities.

tools.name: custom_route_build
tools.description: Break a complex multi-city itinerary into its individual legs and show where a consultant adds value: which legs are routine, which need expertise (Gulf bridge connections, surface sectors, long-haul gaps), and how complex the trip is to ticket. It does not choose airlines and gives no prices - use route_estimate for a price range. Use it for any route with 4+ stops, backtracking, or region combinations that alliance fares can't cover.

cities.description: Ordered list of IATA city/airport codes (e.g. ['LAX', 'NRT', 'BKK', 'CMB', 'NBO', 'LIS', 'LAX'])

budget.description: Budget tier the traveler asked for
